  gender: Male
  ethnicity: South Eastern Asian
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Judge
  trauma_type: Natural disaster
  pcl5: 42

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Emergency Contexts: Ambulances, Olfactory (Hospital): Hospital or antiseptic smell, Weather Similarity: Similar weather conditions to when the event happened
  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Relaxation: avoid relaxing because it feels dangerous, Suppress Thoughts: try hard not think about the trauma, Avoid Going Out: Going out
  Memory: Full Sensory Reliving: When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once, Snapshot Memory: I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind., Visual Memories: My memories of the frightening event are mostly pictures or images.

Vignette:
Rohan still remembers the day the typhoon struck his hometown with eerie precision. He was 25 then, a young lawyer just starting to make a name for himself in the community. The storm's fury was unlike anything he had ever experienced - the howling winds, the relentless rain, and the eerie greenish-black sky that seemed to swallow everything whole. As he huddled with his family in their small apartment, the walls began to shake and the windows shattered, sending shards of glass flying everywhere. Rohan's wife, Nalani, was pregnant at the time, and he recalls the terror that gripped him as he desperately tried to shield her from the debris. The memory of that day has never truly left him. Even now, six years later, the slightest hint of a similar stormy weather pattern - the dark clouds gathering on the horizon, the wind picking up - sends Rohan's heart racing and his mind careening back to that fateful day. He can almost smell the acrid scent of wet earth and ozone that hung in the air as the typhoon made landfall. The antiseptic smell of hospitals also brings it all flooding back, transporting him instantly to the makeshift medical center where he and Nalani were taken after being rescued from their apartment. Rohan has tried to avoid these triggers whenever possible. He steers clear of hospitals, even when his wife or friends are ill, citing work commitments as an excuse. He is equally reluctant to venture out on stormy days, opting instead to stay holed up in his office, pouring over court documents and trying to distract himself from the memories that threaten to overwhelm him. His colleagues have noticed a change in him, remarking on how he seems more withdrawn and isolated than before. But it's not just external triggers that Rohan struggles with - his own thoughts are also a source of torment. He finds himself constantly suppressing memories of the typhoon, trying to push them down into the depths of his mind where they can't hurt him. Yet, these efforts at suppression only seem to make things worse. The memories come back in snapshots - vivid, technicolor images that replay in his mind like a macabre slideshow. He sees himself cowering in fear as the storm rages on outside; he sees Nalani's terrified face, her eyes wide with fear as she clings to him for comfort. Rohan has tried to compensate for these episodes by avoiding relaxation altogether. He convinces himself that if he can just stay busy enough, keep his mind occupied with work and other distractions, the memories won't be able to creep in. But this strategy has come at a cost - his relationships are suffering, particularly with Nalani, who feels increasingly disconnected from her husband. It's only recently, as Rohan's avoidance behaviors have begun to take a toll on his professional life, that he has realized he needs help. As a judge, he is accustomed to being in control, to meting out justice and maintaining order in the courtroom. But when it comes to his own life, he feels powerless against the memories that haunt him. Rohan's greatest fear is that if he doesn't find a way to confront these demons head-on, they will ultimately consume him, destroying everything he holds dear - his marriage, his career, and his very sense of self. With a heavy heart, Rohan has finally made the decision to seek help, hoping against hope that therapy can provide him with the tools he needs to reclaim his life from the grip of trauma. As he sits in his office, staring out at the rain-soaked streets below, he wonders if it's possible to learn to live with these memories, rather than constantly trying to escape them.
